title: Iran Guards say won't reopen Hormuz without US meeting all Tehran's conditions
gist: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say Hormuz stays shut until the US meets every one of Tehran's conditions, declaring the strait 'a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway', while Araghchi denies negotiating with Washington and calls the contacts mere message-exchanges. Iran's demand list spans reparations, sanctions relief, frozen assets, an end to the US counterblockade of Iranian ports and a halt to attacks on its allies — and the Houthis have opened a second front on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast as Turkey pushes to widen the new Sunni defence pact to Egypt.

insights.claim: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they will keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until the United States accepts every one of Tehran's conditions, with no partial or phased reopening on offer.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: An all-or-nothing condition set removes the incremental de-escalation path markets usually price in — the disruption is binary and likely prolonged.
insights.quote: until the enemy accepts all our conditions... the strait is now actually a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway
insights.locator: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Sunday said their strategy

insights.claim: The IRGC has redefined Hormuz as a theatre of war rather than a waterway, which reframes every transiting vessel as an actor in a conflict rather than neutral commerce.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Under a theatre-of-war framing, war-risk underwriting for Hormuz transits should be priced as combat exposure, not incident risk.
insights.quote: the strait is now actually a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway
insights.locator: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Sunday said their strategy

insights.claim: Araghchi publicly denies that Iran is negotiating with the United States, characterising contact as merely 'exchanging messages' through intermediaries.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Denial of negotiations removes the near-term diplomatic catalyst; any 'talks resume' headline would be a genuine surprise, not a continuation.
insights.locator: He denied on Sunday that Iran was negotiating

insights.claim: Araghchi simultaneously calls the Oman transit talks 'approaching the final stages' while making the reopening conditional on compensation for violations of the June agreement.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The 'final stages' language is about lane arrangements, not access — do not trade a Muscat progress headline as a reopening.
insights.quote: is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation
insights.locator: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions with Oman

insights.claim: Security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr's demand list requires an end to war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq before Hormuz reopens.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Four proxy theatres are now formally linked to the shipping file, so any of them can independently block a reopening.
insights.quote: war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq
insights.locator: Iran's security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr

insights.claim: Tehran also demands the lifting of the US counterblockade of Iranian ports, an end to sanctions, release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: This is a full-normalisation ask; the distance to any realistic US concession implies a structurally elevated energy risk premium.
insights.quote: He also demanded the lifting of a US counterblockade of Iranian ports, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage
insights.locator: He also demanded the lifting of a US counterblockade

insights.claim: The United States is running a counterblockade of Iranian ports, meaning the standoff is a two-way maritime siege rather than a one-sided Iranian closure.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Iranian crude exports are constrained too — the supply hit is on both sides of the ledger, which changes the balance math versus a pure Hormuz closure.
insights.locator: He also demanded the lifting of a US counterblockade

insights.claim: Iran wants to charge tolls for Hormuz passage even though international law generally forbids tolling in such waterways, creating a legal impasse at the heart of the dispute.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: No US or Gulf government can formally concede tolling without precedent damage, so any settlement must be informal — a structural reason this drags.
insights.quote: International law generally forbids tolling in such waterways.

insights.claim: Iran has enforced an effective Hormuz blockade since the US and Israel attacked in late February, in a strait that was free to transit before the war.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The baseline has shifted: free transit is now the exception state, so 'normalisation' means undoing six months of enforced routing, not flipping a switch.
insights.quote: Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel attacked in late February
insights.locator: Iran has imposed an effective blockade

insights.claim: Continued attacks in the waterway caused the April ceasefire to collapse, and mediators are pushing both sides back to a June memorandum that set out a path to peace talks.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: One ceasefire has already died on this exact issue — the base rate for the next truce holding without a Hormuz mechanism is low.
insights.quote: led to the collapse of an April ceasefire

insights.claim: The prior Iran-US deal was designed only as a jumping-off point for permanent-settlement talks and delegated Hormuz arrangements to Tehran and Muscat with other Gulf countries, in line with applicable international law.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The framework's legal-conformity clause is precisely what Iran's tolling demand violates — the deal architecture and the demand are incompatible.
insights.quote: in line with the applicable international law

insights.claim: Transit through Hormuz has dropped significantly as Iran targets ships it accuses of skirting its preferred route through Iranian waters.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Volume, not the strait's nominal status, is the tradeable variable; compliance with Iran's routing is now a commercial decision for owners.
insights.quote: transit through Hormuz has dropped significantly
insights.locator: The comments came as transit through Hormuz

insights.claim: The UAE publicly blamed Iran for a missile strike on an ADNOC tanker transiting Hormuz, an unusually direct Emirati attribution.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Direct attribution from Abu Dhabi raises the chance the UAE hardens its alignment against Tehran or seeks the new Sunni pact's cover.
insights.quote: hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC (Abu Dhabi National Oil Company) with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties
insights.locator: The United Arab Emirates' foreign ministry

insights.claim: UKMTO reported a vessel hit by a projectile off Oman in Hormuz with a fire extinguished and no casualties, possibly the same incident as the ADNOC strike.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Incident counts are being double-reported; use UKMTO as the primary series when sizing attack frequency.
insights.quote: a ship was hit by a projectile off Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that was extinguished but no casualties
insights.locator: Later on Saturday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations

insights.claim: Oman condemned repeated attacks on Hormuz shipping without naming Iran while insisting navigation negotiations are 'positive and constructive'.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Muscat is protecting the only live channel; its refusal to attribute is a signal about channel fragility, not about who is shooting.
insights.quote: ongoing negotiations regarding navigation arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz are proceeding in a positive and constructive atmosphere
insights.locator: Oman's foreign ministry on Saturday condemned

insights.claim: The Houthis struck a Saudi oil facility on the Red Sea coast, in an explicit attempt by the Iranian-allied movement to close off a second vital waterway alongside Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Simultaneous pressure on Hormuz and the Red Sea removes the standard bypass route — global crude and product logistics lose both outlets at once.
insights.quote: as the Iranian-allied movement attempts to cut off a second vital waterway
insights.locator: Meanwhile, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels announced

insights.claim: Turkey's Hakan Fidan expects Egypt to join the Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan defence pact, calling Cairo a 'natural partner on all issues'.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Egyptian accession would extend the bloc to the Suez approaches, directly countering the Houthi Red Sea campaign.
insights.quote: I believe that at the next stage Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members
insights.locator: Turkey's foreign minister said on Saturday

insights.claim: A drone struck US assets at an Egyptian Mediterranean port last month, the first such attack on Egyptian territory since the Iran war began.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The conflict has reached the Mediterranean and Egyptian soil — Suez-adjacent and Eastern Med risk is now live, not hypothetical.
insights.quote: A drone struck US assets at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean last month, marking the first drone attack on Egyptian territory since the outbreak of the Iran war.

insights.claim: Fidan says the pact targets no specific country and that no common threat was put in writing, while Pakistan describes it as treating an attack on one as an attack on all.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Ambiguous threat definition plus a hard mutual-defence clause is deliberately untested deterrence — its credibility will be discovered, not declared.
insights.quote: There is no common threat that we have put in writing
insights.locator: Fidan said the agreement does not target a specific country.
